findings.motion: On Passage, H.R. 22, SAVE Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act)
findings.note: Roll call 102. Neal voted Nay on House passage of a bill requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

findings.motion: On Motion to Recommit, H.R. 22, SAVE Act
findings.note: Roll call 101. Neal voted Yea on the motion to recommit the SAVE Act. The clerk page does not give the motion's text, so what the recommit motion would have changed was not read.

findings.motion: On Passage, H.R. 8281, Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act
findings.note: Roll call 345. Neal voted No on House passage of the 2024 SAVE Act, which dealt with documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote.

findings.motion: On Motion to Recommit, H.R. 8281, Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act
findings.note: Roll call 344. Neal voted Yea on the motion to recommit the 2024 SAVE Act. The motion's text was not read.

findings.motion: On Passage, H.R. 1, For the People Act of 2021
findings.note: Roll call 62. Neal voted Yea on House passage of a broad elections bill. The bill's voter ID provisions were not read for this entry, so it is saved only as a general election-law vote.

findings.passage: “There is just been this trend to make voting rights a partisan issue,”
findings.note: Quoted in a news story (reposted on his official site; the outlet name was not shown in the page text read) at a rally marking the 55th anniversary of the Voting Rights Act. He spoke about voting rights and Voting Rights Act re-authorization in general. The story's sentence about state voter ID requirements is the reporter's, not Neal's words, and is not saved.
